nodes.label: Control Panel Vendor (CPV) API
nodes.rationale: the API CIPP uses to add itself to managed tenants and execute actions there; every night at 00:00 UTC permissions are refreshed automatically for all tenants

nodes.label: CPV Reset (Service Principal Management)
nodes.rationale: a CPV reset additionally removes and re-adds the service principal, unlike a plain refresh which only updates permissions

nodes.label: AADSTS50076 MFA Required
nodes.rationale: three causes: no MFA at authorisation, Conditional Access blocking CIPP, or CIPP-SAM app disabled for sign-in in customer tenant

nodes.label: AADSTS7000222 Expired Client Secret
nodes.rationale: app existed over 2 years or secret expired manually, needs new client secret entered via Setup Wizard Manually Enter Credentials

nodes.label: AADSTS50011 Redirect URI Mismatch
nodes.rationale: custom domain added to CIPP but CIPP-SAM app redirect URI not updated to match

nodes.label: High Costs / Unresponsive App
nodes.rationale: restarting the function app during an important task can leave durable functions looping, driving up cost; clearing queues and blobs then restarting resolves it

nodes.label: LastGraphError Property Missing
nodes.rationale: occurs when CIPP cannot write to the errors table or after a failed tenant access check; only fix is clearing the tenant cache

nodes.label: Advanced
nodes.rationale: menu only appears for users granted superadmin access

nodes.label: superadmin Role Requirement
nodes.rationale: as of v8.0 only the superadmin role is needed for these menus; combining it with admin now produces errors, whereas CyberDrain-hosted clients should select both roles on the management portal

nodes.label: Role Impersonation
nodes.rationale: reloads CIPP with only the target role's permissions and tenant scope in force; superadmin cannot be impersonated and impersonation cannot be nested

nodes.label: Permission Rules vs Effective Permissions
nodes.rationale: a pattern-built role is expanded against the current permission list on every evaluation, but the stored Effective Permissions list only records what the patterns matched at last save

nodes.label: Permission Layering (Defaults + Additions)
nodes.rationale: CIPP's own default permissions are always applied and cannot be removed; this page only adds on top of them

nodes.label: Two-Stage Save Process
nodes.rationale: Save Changes on a service principal card only commits to the on-screen set; Save at the bottom submits the whole set to CIPP

nodes.label: Manifest Import/Export
nodes.rationale: permissions the manifest format cannot represent are offered as a separate AdditionalPermissions.json download so nothing is silently lost

nodes.label: Reset to CIPP Defaults
nodes.rationale: removes every additional permission layered on top of the defaults but does not withdraw consent already granted in customer tenants

nodes.label: Directory Role Grant Flow
nodes.rationale: roles are not applied at save time; a tenant is reprocessed once the saved role configuration is newer than that tenant's last permissions refresh, via the next Update Permissions run or a CPV refresh

nodes.label: Compliance Administrator Auto-Grant
nodes.rationale: Compliance Administrator is always granted alongside whatever is selected, whether or not it appears in the list, because CIPP requires it for compliance and Purview functionality

nodes.label: Role Removal Does Not Revoke
nodes.rationale: removing a role from this page stops future grants but does not revoke access already applied in tenants; that has to be removed from the service principal by hand in each tenant

nodes.label: Application Insights Requirement
nodes.rationale: Application Insights must be deployed and the Function App's managed identity needs Reader permissions, or queries fail

nodes.label: As App Permission Context
nodes.rationale: connects using CIPP's application permissions rather than delegated permissions; comparing the two cmdlet sets is the quickest way to isolate a permissions gap

nodes.label: superadmin Role
nodes.rationale: as of v8.0 only the superadmin role is needed for these menus; combining admin and superadmin causes errors, CyberDrain-hosted clients still select both roles on management.cipp.app

nodes.label: Table Maintenance
nodes.rationale: direct read/write access to the raw Azure Storage tables underneath CIPP with no validation, only to be used when directed by CyberDrain support since changes bypass every safeguard and cannot be undone

nodes.label: Row Add/Edit Editor
nodes.rationale: saving writes by PartitionKey/RowKey, so editing either value creates a new row rather than renaming the existing one

nodes.label: cippUser Schema
nodes.rationale: CIPP's built-in schema extension holding JIT administrator state, mailbox type, archive settings and per-user MFA state; CIPP recreates it automatically, it must not be deprecated or removed, and it counts toward the 5-schema-extension limit

nodes.label: Reporting DB Source Type
nodes.rationale: populates a custom data attribute automatically from CIPP's cached reporting DB on a daily schedule; depends on CIPP already holding cached data for the tenant, so values don't appear immediately after saving

nodes.label: Manual Entry Source Type
nodes.rationale: turns the custom data attribute into a technician-facing field on Add/Edit User and the User Patch Wizard instead of syncing automatically

nodes.label: Restore Backup Wizard
nodes.rationale: three-step validate/select-categories/confirm flow so a restore is never applied straight from a click; overwrites the selected categories and cannot be undone

nodes.label: Backup Replication
nodes.rationale: applies to new backups only, nothing existing is copied on enable; CIPP does not manage or prune what it writes to the external container

nodes.label: SAS Token Generation
nodes.rationale: the SAS URL is displayed once and can't be retrieved again; issuing a new one doesn't revoke old ones, and revoking early means rotating the storage account key, which affects the whole CIPP instance

nodes.label: Package Management API
nodes.rationale: requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence on the tenant; the default catalogue listing omits agents so CIPP merges a second agent-package query into one deduplicated view

nodes.label: Template Save/Import/Delete Pattern (Connection Filter)
nodes.rationale: templates capture policy settings for later deployment, created either from an existing tenant policy via 'Create template based on filter' or imported from a community GitHub repo; Save to GitHub / Delete Template actions manage them

nodes.label: Multi-Tenant Deploy Pattern (Connection Filter)
nodes.rationale: deploy form applies settings to one or more selected tenants at once, optionally seeded from a saved template, and reports success/failure per tenant separately

nodes.label: Multi-Tenant Deploy Pattern (Quarantine Policy)
nodes.rationale: same multi-tenant deploy pattern: Select Tenants plus policy fields, Submit applies to all chosen tenants with a per-tenant results panel

nodes.label: Template Save/Import/Delete Pattern (Spamfilter)
nodes.rationale: same template save/reuse pattern as connection filter templates: created from an existing rule or imported from GitHub, managed with Save to GitHub / Delete Template

nodes.label: All Tenants Queue Persistence
nodes.rationale: a single-tenant queue entry drops off the list once processed, but an All Tenants entry stays listed permanently as Deployed and reprocesses every run so tenants added later still get the app; deleting it is the only way to stop that

nodes.label: Enrollment Status Page
nodes.rationale: Add Status Page overwrites the tenant's default ESP (all users and all devices) rather than creating a new one, leaving group-targeted configs alone; submitting it also resets the app-wait scope to all assigned apps and clears scope tags, so an ESP tuned in the Intune admin center should be edited there instead

nodes.label: Multi-Admin Approval
nodes.rationale: an intune access policy holds a protected change pending a second admin's approval instead of applying it immediately; the decision has to come from an account signed into the customer tenant in the approver group, so it can't be made from CIPP (GDAP identity, app identity, and the requestor itself are all refused)

nodes.label: Assignment Filter Template
nodes.rationale: editing a template only changes CIPP's stored copy; it takes effect on the next deployment rather than altering any filter already created in a tenant

nodes.label: Assignment Filter
nodes.rationale: narrows an assignment to the devices or apps matching a rule, so a policy or application assigned to a broad group only reaches the matching subset

nodes.label: BitLocker Recovery Key
nodes.rationale: search hits CIPP's cached escrow records not live graph, so a recently escrowed key or an uncollected device won't be found; Retrieve Key itself is always a live fetch and every retrieval is written to the audit log

nodes.label: Reusable Settings Template
nodes.rationale: holds the configuration for a reusable setting in CIPP so the same setting can be created across tenants, either deployed once from Reusable Settings or kept in place continuously through a standard

nodes.label: Reusable Setting
nodes.rationale: holds a value once so many configuration policies can reference it instead of each carrying its own copy; changing the setting updates every policy that references it

nodes.label: Idempotent Template Deploy Matching
nodes.rationale: CIPP matches an existing tenant object by name against the template: identical is left alone, differing is updated in place, and only a true miss creates a new object, so redeploying a template does not create duplicates

nodes.label: Endpoint Analytics
nodes.rationale: combines startup performance, application reliability, battery health and remote work readiness into a single 0-100 score per device, so an underperforming device can be found without checking each measure separately

nodes.label: Soft-Deleted Directory Object
nodes.rationale: Entra ID keeps a soft-deleted object recoverable for 30 days before automatic permanent removal, so anything still needed must be restored inside that window

nodes.label: Group template Group Type normalization
nodes.rationale: the list column shows the stored value (generic/security/etc) rather than the friendly add-page name; templates saved by older CIPP versions are normalised to these values when the list is built, so an older template still reports a recognisable type

nodes.label: MFA Report
nodes.rationale: reads Entra's registration report plus per-user MFA state plus Conditional Access coverage together because each covers a different set of sign-ins; Covered By CA only reports that a policy targeting the user is enabled, not that it requires MFA for a given sign-in, since a policy scoped to specific apps leaves everything outside that scope unprotected

nodes.label: Sign-in Report
nodes.rationale: saved presets record the number of days rather than resolved dates, so a preset stays relative and always returns the trailing window rather than replaying the same historical week

nodes.label: DLP Policy Templates
nodes.rationale: a DLP policy pending deletion can't be captured as a template because the snapshot wouldn't be deployable; capture is rejected with an explanatory message rather than silently producing a broken template

nodes.label: DLP Policies
nodes.rationale: Enable / TestWithNotifications / TestWithoutNotifications modes let a policy be introduced without enforcing anything yet: neither test mode enforces, they differ only in whether users see policy tips, making them the low-risk way to try a policy on an unfamiliar tenant before moving to Enable

nodes.label: Sensitivity Label Templates
nodes.rationale: a template captured from a live label has its rights management template identifiers stripped because those only mean something in the tenant it came from; the parent label is stored by name and matched again by name in whichever tenant the template is deployed to

nodes.label: Retention Policy Templates
nodes.rationale: Restrictive Retention (Preservation Lock) on a template applies to every tenant it is deployed to and can't be undone; Microsoft doesn't expose the setting in the Purview portal to guard against accidental use, and deploying a locked template here does not ask for confirmation, so the GUID/column is the only checkpoint before deploying

nodes.label: Sensitive Info Type Templates
nodes.rationale: a simple template stores a pattern, confidence level and proximity and has its rule pack built at deploy time; an advanced template carries a captured rule pack XML directly and deploys it as-is, so the two kinds need different previews to show what will actually be detected

nodes.label: CVE Management
nodes.rationale: an exception is recorded in CIPP only and never written back to Defender, so the vulnerability still shows in the Defender portal exactly as before; exceptions change what CIPP reports, not what Microsoft reports. the All Affected Tenants scope currently fails when recording an exception, so All Tenants (Global) or per-tenant recording are the workarounds

nodes.label: Vulnerabilities (TVM)
nodes.rationale: only Affected Devices Count and Affected Devices reflect every device behind a grouped row; the remaining columns are taken from a single one of the grouped findings, so a CVE spanning multiple platforms, vendors or versions shows just one of them as an example rather than the complete picture

nodes.label: Check Alerts
nodes.rationale: the user columns are named "potential" because they carry whatever identity the browser plugin believed it saw at report time, not an authenticated claim, so they are a lead to investigate rather than a confirmed identification

nodes.label: Vulnerability Report
nodes.rationale: the exception columns hold one entry per tenant, so a CVE excepted in several tenants shows several values in a single cell; this page is read-only, defender-cve-exceptions.md is where exceptions are actually worked

nodes.label: Device Compliance
nodes.rationale: this is the directory's view of a device, not Intune's, so a device that hasn't checked in recently can keep reporting its last known compliance state; the last sign-in and sync timestamps should be read alongside compliance before a row is treated as current

nodes.label: MDE Onboarding
nodes.rationale: the connector being configured is a prerequisite, not confirmation of a full Defender deployment; deployment.md is what actually builds the antivirus, exclusion and ASR policies on top of the connector

nodes.label: Breadcrumb Navigation
nodes.rationale: Both display modes ignore the tenant selection when building the trail, so switching tenants doesn't add duplicate entries or embed the tenant name in a label; the trail is hidden entirely where it would say nothing the page doesn't already say (single-entry trails, Home, dashboard).

nodes.label: Keyboard Shortcuts
nodes.rationale: Global shortcuts stay active even while focus is in a text field, so Ctrl+K opens search instead of doing whatever that field would normally do with the keystroke.

nodes.label: Bookmark List Lock
nodes.rationale: The list is locked by default so bookmarks can't be moved or deleted by accident while clicking through the menu; trying to move or remove a locked entry just flashes the padlock instead of acting.

nodes.label: Bookmark Exclusion for Record-Specific Pages
nodes.rationale: Bookmarks store only the page address, so pages whose address identifies a specific record (an individual user or group) are excluded, because the saved address would just reopen an empty page.

nodes.label: Display Mode
nodes.rationale: Stored locally in the browser rather than with the CIPP account, so each browser and device keeps its own light/dark choice.

nodes.label: Release List Cache Fallback
nodes.rationale: The release list is fetched from GitHub and cached; if GitHub can't be reached, the last successfully fetched list is shown instead, so the notes stay readable even when the newest release is missing from the dropdown.

nodes.label: Variable Placeholder Syntax
nodes.rationale: Picking a variable from the % autocomplete list rather than typing it by hand ensures the inserted name always matches exactly what CIPP expects.

nodes.label: Microsoft Graph API - group resource (beta) documentation
nodes.norm_label: microsoft graph api - group resource (beta) documentation

nodes.label: Microsoft Graph API - application resource documentation
nodes.norm_label: microsoft graph api - application resource documentation

nodes.label: View App Registration
nodes.rationale: Rotating a client secret creates a replacement and deletes the original as soon as the replacement exists, so anything still using the old value stops working until it is updated with the new one.

nodes.label: Permission Sets
nodes.rationale: Editing a permission set changes it for every application template that references it, but the change does not reach tenants on its own since applications already deployed keep the permissions they were granted until the template is deployed again; deleting a set leaves any referencing template without its permissions.

nodes.label: Permission Set Reference
nodes.rationale: enterprise app template references a permission set by ID rather than copying it, so editing the set changes what the template grants on its next deployment

nodes.label: Manifest Multi-Tenant Rejection
nodes.rationale: multi-tenant manifests rejected on purpose: deploying a manifest creates a new app in the target tenant, and a multi-tenant one made this way would be consentable from outside that tenant

nodes.label: Live Graph Query
nodes.rationale: reads live from Microsoft rather than CIPP's own storage, so it reflects the tenant's current Entra retention period, not CIPP history; no data until a tenant is selected

nodes.label: Location Information
nodes.rationale: geolocation is an estimate from IP registration data, treat as a signal rather than proof, particularly for mobile and hosting addresses

nodes.label: Identifier Resolution
nodes.rationale: object IDs resolved to display names both as property values and inside longer strings, original identifier on hover; unresolved identifiers marked as such rather than left silently raw

nodes.label: Search Window State Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Planned/Created/Downloaded/Retry/DeadLetter/Skipped; Skipped means unified auditing was off for the tenant and that period's audit data cannot be recovered later

nodes.label: Targeting Actions
nodes.rationale: Deploy to Custom Group and Assign to All Users both replace the method's include targets rather than adding to them

nodes.label: FIDO2 Enable Policy Defaults
nodes.rationale: Enable Policy turns on attestation enforcement and self-service registration as CIPP's defaults; use Configure afterwards if either should be off

nodes.label: Include All Users Fallback
nodes.rationale: saving with Include all users off and nothing chosen in include fields does not scope the campaign to nobody, it falls back to targeting all users; use Campaign state Disabled to stop the prompt instead

nodes.label: Standard Overwrite Conflict
nodes.rationale: the Authenticator registration standard writes the same campaign settings, so changes made on this page are overwritten the next time that standard runs

nodes.label: Domains
nodes.rationale: Verification only succeeds once the ownership DNS record has propagated; running Verify Domain before then returns an error rather than queuing a retry, so the record must be published and given time to propagate first.

nodes.label: Microsoft Graph API - domain resource documentation
nodes.norm_label: microsoft graph api - domain resource documentation

nodes.label: All Tenants Nightly Cache Rows
nodes.community_name: All Tenants Nightly Cache Rows cluster

nodes.label: Tenant Cache Refresh
nodes.rationale: tenants served from CIPP's own cache rather than read from Partner Center on every load; clear the tenant cache from Settings to queue a background refresh

nodes.label: GDAP Permission Warning
nodes.rationale: portal links open using the currently logged in user's own partner credentials and GDAP permissions, not the CIPP service account

nodes.label: Relationship Health Dropout
nodes.rationale: a tenant that repeatedly fails to return data from Graph accumulates errors against its record and is eventually dropped from the standard tenant list

nodes.label: GDAP Relationship Age Evaluation
nodes.rationale: measured from the activation date of the tenant's oldest active GDAP relationship, so age does not reset when a newer relationship is accepted; terminated/expired relationships ignored, and direct tenants with no active GDAP relationship never match an age rule

nodes.label: Multi-Tenant Named Location Creation
nodes.rationale: not limited to the selected tenant, creates the same named location in each chosen tenant as separate objects sharing only a name; later edits must be made per tenant

nodes.label: Custom Test Risk Level
nodes.rationale: risk is assigned by whoever wrote the test, reflects their own severity judgement rather than a microsoft or cipp classification

nodes.label: Anonymised Usage Reports
nodes.rationale: a tenant-wide m365 setting hashes user/site names in usage reports instead of showing real names; the fix is the Enable Usernames standard on the tenant, not something cipp can toggle itself

nodes.label: Domain Analyser Data Refresh Mechanism
nodes.rationale: the analyser doesn't query graph for the domain list directly, it reads cipp's cached tenant data then runs its own dns lookups; a domain has to reach the cache before the analyser can see it and re-running the analysis won't pull in a domain the cache hasn't collected yet
nodes.community_name: Domain Analyser Data Refresh Mechanism cluster

nodes.label: Domain Analyser Excluded Domains
nodes.rationale: microsoft and known cloud signature/voice provider domains are never analysed since their dns records are outside your control; the same exclusions apply to the Add DKIM standard

nodes.label: Restore to This Version
nodes.rationale: destructive, deletes every version newer than the one restored to; use Compare to Latest to inspect without discarding

nodes.label: Have I Been Pwned Check
nodes.rationale: email lookups need a have-i-been-pwned API key configured on the instance; missing key fails with a connection error instead of an empty result; CyberDrain hosted tenants get a complimentary key

nodes.label: Tenant Breach Lookup
nodes.rationale: background per-domain search; results only write back when the breached-account count for a domain changed since the last search, so an unchanged table does not mean the search failed

nodes.label: New Mailbox Restore
nodes.rationale: restoring into the target's primary mailbox without Target Root Folder merges source content into the existing folders, which is difficult to unpick afterwards; set a target root folder to keep restored mail separate and easy to remove

nodes.label: Message Viewer
nodes.rationale: runs entirely in the browser; the message is never uploaded to CIPP or sent to Microsoft, no tenant is involved, and nothing is written to the logs, which makes it safe for a reported phishing sample

nodes.label: CIPP Template Source Type
nodes.rationale: templates are read as stored; tenant variable replacement and reusable settings are not resolved because no tenant is chosen for this source type

nodes.label: Settings Catalog Comparison
nodes.rationale: type-aware comparison matches settings by definition, shows setting names and choice option names instead of raw IDs/values, and expands nested group settings; Defender onboarding/offboarding blobs are skipped since they are unique per tenant and would otherwise always show as a difference

nodes.label: Application Approval
nodes.rationale: a one-off action against the tenants you pick; it does not remediate tenants added later, unlike the App Approval standard which keeps the deployment enforced over time

nodes.label: Manual Configuration
nodes.rationale: selecting permissions by hand applies Microsoft Graph permissions only; if the application needs permissions on any other resource API, leave Copy permissions from the existing application enabled, or use a template

nodes.label: Individual Domain Check
nodes.rationale: the user is responsible for ensuring their use of this tool complies with applicable laws, registry terms, and the terms of service for the Google and Cloudflare DNS APIs

nodes.label: Tenant Lookup
nodes.rationale: queries endpoints Microsoft exposes publicly, so it works against any tenant without a GDAP relationship and without the tenant existing in CIPP; branding is a helpful signal, not proof of identity

nodes.label: Build: Dev Container
nodes.rationale: cancels an in-flight dev build when a newer commit is pushed to dev via a concurrency group; --pull ensures the floating 8.0-* base image tag is re-resolved so runtime patches (e.g. a six High-CVE 8.0.28->8.0.29 bump) land in published images instead of sitting unapplied

nodes.label: regression
nodes.rationale: regression gate for the Azure-native branch: compiles the AzureTables configuration and runs the combined-role E2E suite (Azurite + orchestrator + scheduler + realtime + API dispatch) on PRs to main/dev and pushes to dev; doc-only changes do not trigger it

nodes.label: lint (format + analyzers)
nodes.rationale: runs before build so a formatting-only mistake fails in ~30s instead of after the E2E suite; asserts zero build warnings without TreatWarningsAsErrors so transient SDK warnings do not fail builds

nodes.label: global.json SDK pin
nodes.rationale: no dotnet-version is set in setup-dotnet on purpose; global.json pins the SDK and setup-dotnet honours it, keeping CI, build/Dockerfile and developer machines on one Roslyn + analyzer set

nodes.label: Base Image Re-resolution (pull: true)
nodes.rationale: pull:true forces re-resolving the .NET base image on every build instead of reusing runner/GHA cache, so a patched runtime (e.g. 8.0.28->8.0.29, six High CVEs) gets picked up automatically; Dockerfile floats on the 8.0-* tag but that only works if the tag is actually re-resolved

nodes.label: Craft Contributor License Agreement
nodes.rationale: contributions auto-transfer copyright to CyberDrain with no signature; enables CyberDrain to relicense including custom/commercial licenses for sponsors

nodes.label: Craft
nodes.rationale: lightweight ASP.NET Core runtime hosting PowerShell modules as HTTP endpoints, background workers, orchestrators and scheduled tasks; replaces Azure Functions for containerized deployments

nodes.label: Craft.Services Namespace
nodes.rationale: everything in Services/Bridges plus PowerShellRunnerService stays in namespace Craft.Services permanently; downstream PowerShell reaches these types by fully-qualified name; renaming compiles cleanly but fails at runtime with Unable to find type, and TypeForwardedTo cannot rescue it since these types all live in Craft.dll; the containing folder is free to move, the namespace is not

nodes.label: Microsoft.Azure.Functions.PowerShellWorker.HttpResponseContext
nodes.rationale: namespace must match the real Azure Functions worker type because hosted-app routers match on PSObject.TypeNames; all four properties (StatusCode, Body, Headers, ContentType) reach the wire so a handler can redirect

nodes.label: Craft.Hosting.HandlerHeaders
nodes.rationale: normalises header values before they are written: strips CR/LF, drops empty values instead of emitting empty headers, and refuses headers Kestrel computes for itself (Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, Connection, Host); headers are cached and replayed alongside status and body so a cached redirect still redirects

nodes.label: PowerShellContractTests
nodes.rationale: asserts every [Craft.Services.*] type PowerShell calls by name still exists, is public, and that nothing unrelated has drifted into that frozen namespace; the only thing turning a downstream-breaking rename into a build failure instead of a runtime one

nodes.label: ConfigurationReferenceTests
nodes.rationale: asserts every default documented in appsettings.example.jsonc still matches the C# default it claims to document, so the example cannot rot into a lie

nodes.label: appsettings.example.jsonc
nodes.rationale: annotated reference listing every config key and its default; documentation only, the .jsonc extension keeps it out of the build glob since it contains comments

nodes.label: Docker build --pull base image floating tag
nodes.rationale: the base image tags float on the 8.0-* minor so .NET runtime security patches are picked up automatically, but only if the tag is re-resolved; without --pull Docker reuses a months-old local base image, and those CVEs live in the shared runtime the base image ships so no package bump fixes them and dotnet list package --vulnerable never reports them; CI sets pull: true
nodes.norm_label: docker build --pull base image floating tag

nodes.label: Security Policy
nodes.rationale: report via security@cyberdrain.com or Discord admins; reports published after resolution; $50 bounty for critical RCE/data-leak bugs, swag otherwise

nodes.label: wizard state object
nodes.rationale: everything interactive on the page derives from `wizard` via decideWizardState()/applyWizardState(); nothing is enabled or disabled ad hoc and no control depends on a single un-retried network call. originally btn-seed shipped disabled and was only enabled by one branch of one fetch whose only error handler was console.error, so a slow container, storage timeout, or non-JSON error body left the page permanently inert with no explanation

nodes.label: decideWizardState()
nodes.rationale: pure branch table (no DOM, no fetch, no globals) mapping what's known about the host to what the wizard should look like; extracted for the same reason SetupGate is - the branch table is the whole behaviour and the part that broke. covered by tests/setup-wizard/

nodes.label: statusReadError()
nodes.rationale: returns null when a /api/setup/status response is usable, else a short reason; the empty-200 case is not hypothetical - a route bound MapGet's RequestDelegate overload and wrote nothing at all, so res.ok was true, there was no Content-Type, and res.json() threw on an empty body. checking res.ok alone would not have caught it

nodes.label: refreshStatus()
nodes.rationale: the initial read and the background refresh are the same operation, so a failed first attempt recovers on its own rather than bricking the page for the rest of the session

nodes.label: What You Get (fork clone, dev stack, graph, CLAUDE.md)
nodes.norm_label: what you get (fork clone, dev stack, graph, claude.md)

nodes.label: cipp-openapi-v2.json
nodes.rationale: auto-generated OpenAPI 3.1 snapshot of the CIPP API (static analysis of backend+frontend, last generated 2026-03-02); point-in-time, not regenerated by this repo's tooling - as of 2026-07-21 covers 488 of 618 http entrypoints (134 newer ones missing, 4 spec paths no longer map to an http entrypoint)

nodes.label: fnmatch-based ignore matching
nodes.rationale: `*` crosses `/`; root-anchored patterns (leading /) match the scan-root-relative path as a full string, unanchored patterns match every path component at every depth

nodes.label: detect merges scan root's .gitignore
nodes.rationale: the workspace's CIPP/ gitignore line would collapse the corpus to nothing, so .graphifyignore carries an unanchored !CIPP negation (last-match-wins) before the anchored excludes - that line must be kept

nodes.label: nested .gitignore/.graphifyignore not read
nodes.rationale: _load_graphifyignore walks upward only, so nested ignore files inside subdirectories are not read when scanning from a parent root; the committed root .graphifyignore is the single scope authority

nodes.label: build_merge does not persist to disk
nodes.rationale: the docstring claims otherwise; every caller must to_json afterward
nodes.norm_label: build_merge does not persist to disk

nodes.label: build_merge replace-on-re-extract
nodes.rationale: all base-graph nodes/edges whose source_file matches any incoming one are dropped before merge - this is why route edges use the synthetic source graph-tools/route-links

nodes.label: to_json() shrink guard (#479)
nodes.rationale: returns False (writing nothing) when the new graph has fewer nodes than the existing file unless force=True

nodes.label: update.py/routelink/craftlink force=True wrapping
nodes.rationale: wrap to_json with their own 10 percent threshold + force=True, because build_merge fuzzy dedup can shrink a merge by a few nodes and force=False would silently drop the pass

nodes.label: recluster uses force=False deliberately
nodes.rationale: node count never changes during a recluster, so the shrink guard is meant to stay armed

nodes.label: graphify.extract.extract multiprocessing
nodes.rationale: uses multiprocessing - any calling script needs `if __name__ == '__main__':` on windows

nodes.label: zero-node source files retried (#1666)
nodes.rationale: zero-node source files are reported and retried each run; the warning is benign
